subject: Creativity
title: Elon Musk: First-Principles Thinking
description: A 60-second lesson on Elon Musk: First-Principles Thinking.

hook.text: Rockets cost $65 million. Musk asked: what do the raw materials cost? Answer: 2% of that. SpaceX was born.

buildup.text: First-principles thinking strips a problem to its fundamental truths — then rebuilds solutions from scratch.

discovery.text: Instead of buying rockets, Musk built them. Instead of buying batteries, he built a factory. Cost collapsed.

twist.text: This approach isn't new. Aristotle described first principles 2,300 years ago. Musk just applied it to engineering.

climax.text: SpaceX's reusable rockets cut launch costs by 90% — an impossibility according to every incumbent aerospace company.

punchline.text: The most creative question is: 'Why do we do it this way?'

quiz.question: What percentage of rocket cost were raw materials when Musk investigated?

details.summary: Elon Musk applies first principles thinking: breaking problems down to their fundamental truths and reasoning up from there rather than reasoning by analogy to what already exists. This approach led him to rethink rocket costs, battery economics, and manufacturing processes from scratch.
details.whyItMatters: First principles thinking is a learnable creative approach that challenges assumptions in any field. It explains how Musk's companies achieved results that industry experts declared impossible.
takeaways: First principles thinking questions every assumption rather than accepting conventions
SpaceX reduced rocket costs by rebuilding from fundamental physics and materials
The approach is learnable and applicable beyond technology

faq.question: What is first principles thinking?
faq.answer: It means breaking a problem down to its most basic truths and building solutions from those truths rather than from existing solutions. Instead of asking how to improve a rocket, Musk asked what a rocket's raw materials cost and worked from there.

faq.question: How did this approach apply to SpaceX?
faq.answer: The aerospace industry said rockets could not be made cheaper. Musk calculated the raw material cost of a rocket was about two percent of the purchase price. By manufacturing in-house, reusing boosters, and questioning every inherited assumption, SpaceX cut launch costs by over 90 percent.
